analysis.title: Situation Room: Flows pause
key_insights: US HG bond fund and ETF inflows fell to +$1.22bn in the week ending Oct 21, from +$4.32bn the prior week. IG corporates are about a third of HG AUM, which implies roughly $0.4bn of IG demand.
HG ETF inflows slowed to +$4.97bn from +$6.31bn, while HG fund outflows grew to -$3.76bn from -$1.99bn, the biggest fund outflow since April 2025.
Short-term HG inflows moderated to +$0.44bn from +$1.77bn, and ex-short-term HG inflows to +$0.77bn from +$2.55bn.
Equity fund inflows dropped to +$9.06bn from +$43.91bn the prior week.

HY outflows continued at -$0.65bn (prior -$1.24bn), while loan inflows improved to +$0.26bn from +$0.03bn. Muni inflows weakened to +$0.67bn from +$4.51bn, and global EM bond outflows continued at -$0.66bn (prior -$0.67bn).
Money markets took in +$25.27bn after a -$53.90bn outflow the week before.

Year to date as of Oct 21, flows are 8.3% of AUM for HG ($423.8bn), 0.1% for HY ($0.4bn), 10.8% for loans ($19.2bn), 1.4% for equities ($398.7bn) and 8.9% for all fixed income ($737.8bn). Loans have the biggest YTD inflows at 11.3% of AUM in the chart series, followed by all fixed income at 8.7%.
Cumulative flows since 10/2024 reached 26% of AUM for HG, 10% for HY, 47% for equities and 8% for loans as of Oct 21.
IG issuance was zero on Oct 22, with $23.7bn week to date and $68.4bn month to date. This week's new issues are trading 3bps tighter on average from pricing.

Estimated IG dealer inventories of US issuer bonds rose to -$4.3bn on Oct 22 from -$8.2bn on Oct 14. Inventory DV01 rose to -$9.3mn from -$12.2mn. Inventories have generally stayed negative since Oct 2025.
Estimated IG dealer inventories rose $557mn on Oct 22, $5,671mn over the prior week and $1,381mn over four weeks. By sector on Oct 22, Banks/Brokers rose $355mn and Energy fell $229mn.
Daily HG fund flows were -$389mn on Oct 21 versus -$173mn on Oct 20. Average daily HG inflow was $630mn in October versus $903mn in September.
HG fund flows have been decoupled from returns since around Oct 2024, though they followed returns from Oct 2023.
Net foreign buying of 10yr+ IG over 12 days rose $161mn over the past 5 business days ending Oct 22, while 30yr Treasury yields were unchanged.
risk_factors: HG fund outflows are accelerating even as ETF inflows continue.
Weekly inflows slowed across HG bonds and equities, and HY outflows continued.
charts_described: Exhibit 10 states HG cumulative flows increased to 26% of AUM as of Oct-21 (two years since 10/2024).
Exhibit 12 states equities cumulative flows steadily increased to 47% of AUM as of Oct-21 since 10/2024.
Exhibit 21 states HG fund flows tend to follow returns since Oct-2023 but have been decoupled since around Oct-2024.
vol_and_positioning: HG fund outflows of -$3.76bn were the largest since April 2025, while ETF inflows held at +$4.97bn.
Weekly equity inflows fell about 79% from the prior week, to +$9.06bn from +$43.91bn.
Money market funds took in +$25.27bn after a -$53.90bn outflow the prior week.
IG dealer inventories are estimated at -$4.3bn, which is still net short.
